title: 1959 AHSME Problem 9
statement: A farmer divides his herd of \(n\) cows among his four sons so that one son gets one-half the herd, a second son one-fourth, a third son one-fifth, and the fourth son \(7\) cows. Then \(n\) is:

solutions.text:
The first three sons receive \[ \frac12+\frac14+\frac15=\frac{19}{20} \] of the herd. Thus the remaining \(\frac{1}{20}\) of the herd is \(7,\) so \(n=140.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Add the three fractional shares of the herd
The fraction left over corresponds to \(7\) cows
